geometry_edits.rationale: Retarget the public-space controller from a generic court to a clearer courtyard/open-threshold device that can respond to the access edge.
Expand the carved public space so it becomes a readable ground response rather than a narrow incision.
Align the courtyard opening to the verified access side in the program frame so the frontage becomes semantically active.
Keep the existing aggregate structure while allowing the revised courtyard operator to drive the final public threshold.

graph_edits.rationale: Shift the dominant mass away from a generic bar toward a split-wing / courtyard-capable primary form so the access edge can be articulated without losing the main anchor.
Keep the primary mass aligned to the long axis so the courtyard or notch can read clearly across all views.
Create a more legible spatial split to introduce public void without over-fragmenting the mass.
Preserve a dominant connected gesture so the building remains one coherent massing idea after carving.
Convert the subtraction from a small cave-like cut into a true public courtyard logic that can own the ground threshold.
Widen the open-space figure so it reads as usable public space rather than a decorative nick.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact rectilinear bar with a single carved/selected void and some upper bending, so it is not incoherent, but it is too close to a generic box for the stated neighborhood-living brief. The four views are consistent enough to avoid a pure one-view failure, and the green parcel is mostly respected, but the dominant gesture does not yet create a convincing active street threshold on the verified access edge. The blue frontage is answered only weakly: the mass mostly seals the edge rather than expressing a clear public seam, court, or undercut aligned with access. Sectionally, the form behaves more like a lifted bent slab/canopy than a grounded mixed-use building with a legible public ground relation, so program_fit_hard_pass fails. The reference set consistently supports one transferable principle: keep a dominant mass but carve a more explicit public void/entry notch at the access side and preserve a clear upper-vs-ground hierarchy. The best corrective direction is to strengthen the public threshold and reduce the box-like character while keeping the single dominant bar as anchor.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Use a dominant mass with a carved central void and a legible upper connector to create a public threshold.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with a void and elevated connections can support a clear hierarchy of ground and upper mass.

warnings: Parcel containment appears acceptable in the rendered views, so the failure is semantic rather than a hard containment breach.
The verified access edge is not met with a sufficiently legible public opening.
The silhouette is coherent, but the section does not yet read as neighborhood-living with an active ground condition.
Avoid over-fragmenting the mass; the form needs one stronger anchor and one clearer carved public void.
